products.name: Box AI
products.note: Enterprise content AI; metadata; governance; compliance; retention policies

reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box describes itself as an AI-powered content management, workflow and collaboration platform, which it calls Intelligent Content Management. Per its site, the platform is built around unstructured data such as sales presentations, product specs, employee handbooks, lease agreements and finance documents, and combines access, sharing, editing and co-creation with enterprise-grade security and compliance. The company was founded in 2005, is headquartered in Redwood City, CA, USA, is a public company trading under the ticker BOX, and has CIK 0001372612.

Box AI is its tracked product, listed in the Notes, Knowledge and Meetings category and described as enterprise content AI with metadata, governance, compliance and retention policies. The site says Box AI draws on leading models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google for summaries, analysis and recommendations, and that Box AI Studio lets customers customize agents to streamline workflows. Box also describes AI-driven security with deep learning-based malware detection, automated classification and granular access controls, compliance tools for requirements such as GDPR, HIPAA and FINRA, and AI-driven e-signature workflows. It states that Box was named a Leader with the highest scores possible in 13 criteria, including innovation, vision, security and AI/ML.

Its most recent revenue filing is a 10-K for the period ending 2026-01-31, reporting $1,177,253,000. Box's law exposure is recorded in California, with a count of 281. In the MCP server registry, its entry is associated with servers including ai.clize/inbox, ai.ironshard/agent-storage-sandbox, ai.powerline/inbox-preview, ai.slidingbox/hydrate-dehydrate, ai.smithery/smithery-toolbox, ai.thoughtbox.api/thoughts and bot.mailbox/mailbox.
